And in the first paragraph, it says: "We have received some assessments that the military police of the administration does not have under its control the security situation in the town of Mostar." My question, Mr. Vidovic: Did you know of such assessments of the work of the military police in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the first part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That the assessment was that the military police did not have under its control the security situation in the town of Mostar. It's a report from mid-March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to intervene because this document is already an exhibit. I think it was brought through documentary evidence. But on the document, it says "1992," and then next to that it is handwritten "1993." And this signature is not Mr. Coric's signature. So perhaps my colleague has some additional knowledge as to whose signature this is and which year this is. Perhaps the witness knows. Perhaps the witness should be asked what year it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in 1992 there was no HVO yet, so I believe that this is pure obstruction of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, Mr. Vidovic, 5D2113, 2113. This is a report that was signed by the chief of the Military Police Administration. The date is the 4th of June, 1993. And in paragraph 4, it says: "On the 31st of May, 1993, the military police received the order that as of the 1st of June, 1993, it has to place under its absolute control the part of town that was under the control of HVO units. The order was issued because there was a great deal of crime and many apartments were robbed." Mr. Vidovic, were you aware of this task of the military police of the HVO in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to skip a document, and let us look at document P4058. The first part of the report has to do with the Section for Combatting Crime. And then in the second part, we see the section for Mostar. My first question, Mr. Vidovic, has to do with the part of the report that is on page 5 of the Mostar report. In English, it is page 13. Roughly around the middle of the page, it says, and I quote: "That is how we encounter organised crime. The perpetrators are groups of armed men who often introduce themselves as members of the military police, members of the so-called ATGs." Tell us, Mr. Vidovic, did you write this part of the report, you or your associates?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Croatian, it's page 5, if I understand you correctly. I've just found it, so could you tell me where it is?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The middle of the page. It's enough for you to listen to me, and you don't really have to read it word for word. So groups of --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how we encounter -- ah, yes, I see. Could you please repeat your question so I'll answer it then?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you compile this report, together with your associates?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On the next page, roughly around the middle of the page - it is 14 in English, page 14 in English - certain characteristics of crimes in Mostar are being referred to. Tell us, Mr. Vidovic, did you make an effort to devote particular attention to dealing with crimes when the victims were ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that yesterday. We treated all perpetrators of crimes equally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document, among the conclusions, there is a reference under number 6, at the end of the document, that a co-ordinating body should be established to unify the activity of this section of Mostar and the corresponding sections in the Police Administration and police stations in all areas of police activity. Mr. Vidovic, tell us, did you truly make an effort to enhance your work and co-operation with the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there were several meetings that were held in order to achieve that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the next document, 5D4117. Tell us, Mr. Vidovic, if you know, what kind of a meeting was this and what kind of a record is this?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the hosts were the MUP on one occasion. This time, we are hosting this meeting where the military police and the Crime Department of the MUP are meeting again with the representatives of the judiciary organs and the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what is the subject of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same like at the first meeting; analysing the state of crime in town and proposing measures needed to curb the situation in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, P4111, P4111. It is a record of a working meeting that was held --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your time is up now, and we will finish with this document. It's just about time to stop anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So this is a record from a work meeting held on the 11th of August, 1993, in Mostar. The topic is the state of law and order in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I would like to draw your attention, inter alia, to the conclusion under number 3; namely, that it is particularly necessary to link up and place under one's control various groups that are outside full command control. Tell me, Mr. Vidovic, can you give me a comment on this? Does this have to do with the groups that were outside any kind of control, and that it is really out of avarice that they were committing crimes in the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO VIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to your instructions, I have concluded my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I know that you have questions, but I'm afraid that we are going to finish and I'm now going to say something that I think is very important. We have no transcript from pages 1 through 8 today. I think that this is a technical problem that we have to resolve at this session, because the transcript starts only on page 8. It is important so that we would have the complete statement and testimony of this witness. So I would like that to be dealt with before we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, there is a virus that is having an impact on the entire computer network of the Tribunal, and the technicians are doing their best to try and solve the problem. That said, we were able to follow on LiveNote the transcript page by page, so everyone was able to follow the questions and the answers today. We hope that the technicians will be able to solve this problem. Whatever the case may be, we still have the audio recording. Just to finish off, I would like to ask Mr. Pusic's counsel whether he has any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will give you our answer tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have all night to think about it. We shall meet again tomorrow. As you know, we shall be sitting in the morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The Accused Praljak and Pusic not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
